subject: computer
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Tell the story of computers, starting from the abacus in the late 1930s
Know that computers are grouped into five generations by their hardware
Compare the five generations of computers
Name the characteristics and limitations of computers
Keep up with new technology developments
Define software as the programs that make a computer do its tasks
Tell system software from application software
Name the other types: operation support, utility, general purpose and customised software
Back up files
Scan a drive, folder or file for problems
Use the defragmentation utility
Use advanced formatting: format painter, subscript, superscript and shadow
Use find, replace and insert tools
Add headers and footers
Insert columns, page breaks and line breaks
Set tabs, indents, margins, page orientation and page size
Insert shapes and pictures, and add borders and shading
Build a presentation with a built-in template
Change the colour scheme and background colour
Set the alignment of text on slides
Add clip art, WordArt and shapes
Apply formatting effects so that key points stand out
Explain programming as turning steps into instructions a computer can run
Find their way around the Scratch screen
Use basic motion, pen and sound blocks
Make simple games, stories or art in Scratch
Build logical thinking
Name the ways to connect to the internet: dial-up, broadband and wireless
Use internet services safely
Follow netiquette when communicating online
Act as a responsible netizen
